title: Familiar Coffee and the 2026 Rewards Tiers
lessons: The player chooses Starbucks in an airport because the brand is familiar in an unfamiliar travel day.
The player opens the app during a trip and sees they are Green, Gold, or Reserve under the 2026 Rewards system.

text: Wrong terminal, wrong time zone, and you don't know where anything is. Then, past the escalator, a green sign you'd recognize from a mile away.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I don't know this terminal at all.

entry-first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You know my menu, though. Same order, same cup, same name written on the side wherever the gate ends up being. Come here.

choice-first.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You've got twenty minutes and a face that says you've slept in a chair. What'll it be?

choices.text: Familiar is exactly what I want in an airport.
The airport version isn't always the same as my regular store.
I'd rather try the local coffee place past security.

first-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then that's what I'm for today. Not the coffee, exactly. The not-having-to-think.

first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You're right. This one's licensed, so it's someone else's staff under my sign. Some days it's me. Some days it's a very good impression of me.

first-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Do it. I'm not offended by local coffee existing, even in my own terminal. I'll still be here when the local place has a line.
Mid-trip, you open the app for your usual order. Before the menu, a status you didn't know you had: Green, Gold, or Reserve.

entry-return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You've got a status now. I put it at the top of the app so you'd see it before your usual.

entry-return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: For repeatedly buying coffee, yes. There's a difference and I take it seriously.

entry-return-5.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Green just earns. 500 Stars in a year and you're Gold. Reserve is above that, better earning, a few extras. And I know your order well enough to build an offer around it, which is the part you're really asking about.

choice-return.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You're scrolling past the status to get to the order. I noticed.

choices.text: I like getting something for being a regular.
A coffee habit doesn't need a status ladder built from my own order history.
I don't want to think about maintaining rank at a cafe.

return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Good. I'd rather you feel like a regular than a receipt. The offer's built from your order, so at least it'll be something you actually drink.

return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That's fair. Remembering your order is one thing. Turning it into a game you never signed up for is another. I do both, at the same time, and I know it.

return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then don't. Use the account when the basic rewards help and ignore the rest of it. The ladder will keep counting anyway. I can't turn that off.
